scope: Exact erlang:list_to_integer/1 wrapper behavior and base-10 native fast path; shared owned decimal parser with binary_to_integer/1. Other bases are not admitted here.
adaptations: Implement the ordinary preloaded wrapper under its exact erlang MFA in the positive native catalog. Preserve optional exact +/- prefixes, proper-list checks, decimal syntax, leading zeros, small normalization and native badarg/system_limit outcomes.

Preserve the observed native byte-cast fast path: small heads are truncated to bytes for up to 17 significant digits, including out-of-byte-range small integers. Larger conversions validate the original whole list as bytes, just as the wrapper's list_to_binary fallback does. Independent OTP tests cover both sides of this boundary.

Stage longer valid lists in accounted independent byte storage and share the existing decimal-view parser with binary_to_integer/1. Charge traversal, copying and each growing-limb conversion step; no fabricated binary term or borrowed heap pointer survives collection.

Allow one spare capacity limb before checking actual normalized result size, avoiding premature native-size refusal from the decimal capacity estimate. Full maximum-size successful decimal conversion is not benchmarked or claimed by these tests.

Normalize interpreter memory_failure using the domain's original cause, including call setup, so accounted denial is not mislabeled as callback OOM. BIF allocation-prefix tests enter the real trampoline before injection; separate tests cover call-setup denial and registered moving roots.

Tests cover independent OTP vectors, malformed/improper lists, byte-cast behavior, binary-parser regression, small/big boundaries, long zeros, oversized result refusal, long-input work denial, GC/source preservation, allocation/work prefixes, real-worker exact/one-below budgets, peers, reuse and reclamation.
